Advances: specled.mix_tasks

From specled_-hj4.1 round-3 verification note (2026-07-25). Mix.Tasks.Spec.Check validate_base!/2 (spec.check.ex, added in hj4.1 to print a fail verdict before raising) is a logic-for-logic copy of BranchCheck private validate_base!/2 (branch_check.ex:635-651), differing only in raise type and message tail. The two will silently diverge if the C13 commit-only ref rule changes. Expose one public validator both call. Related advisory: next.ex:313 suggested_commands_with_protocol/1 appends the read-protocol sentence to any non-empty commands list and renders it as a bullet inside commands: — revisit only if that list is ever machine-consumed.

DISPOSITION CONFIRMED 2026-07-25 (see ticket comments): IMPLEMENT AS WRITTEN, not moot. Fold in the two same-class duplication findings:
- CF4: spec.check.ex re-implements TaskArgs.validate!/3's own head match purely to position the verdict print before the raise. Cleanest fix: convert TaskArgs.validate!/3 (or add a sibling) returning :ok | {:error, message} so verdict and raise derive from one evaluation; spec.validate.ex:126-131 shows the print-inside-failure-clause pattern.
- CF6: print_verdict/2 in both task modules matches options positionally so option ORDER is load-bearing and same-named helpers have INCOMPATIBLE option lists across the two modules. Read options via Keyword.get/3.
- Also from the same review: spec.validate.ex sort_findings_for_display/1 re-types the exact four-element tuple of sort_key/1 twenty lines above. Compose rather than duplicate.

NOTE (from specled_-0x4.2 verification, 2026-07-26): spec.check now emits tier=usage for its pre-flight rejections via print_usage_verdict/0. spec.validate's own pre-flight min-strength rejection still emits `spec.validate result=fail tier=validate error_findings=0` (spec.validate.ex:229, pinned at spec_tasks_test.exs:943) — the same dishonesty 0x4.2 fixed for spec.check. Fixing that for spec.validate is IN SCOPE here if and only if the shared-validator/CF4/CF6 work touches those sites anyway and the mix_tasks grammar you inherit already names tier=usage; keep it minimal and update the pinned test + spec scenario accordingly. If it turns into its own project, defer with a follow-up ticket instead.

## Spec co-change authorization

Editing .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md and the tool-managed baseline .spec/realization_hashes.json (via documented regeneration) is IN SCOPE. Minimal prose-only reconciliation edits to OTHER subject specs are authorized ONLY when the spec gate demands them (branch_guard_missing_subject_update) — smallest edit that keeps the gate green, and every file such a note names must genuinely be in your diff. This authorization comes before any scope warning below.

## Allowed touches

- lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex
- lib/mix/tasks/spec.validate.ex
- lib/spec_led_ex/branch_check.ex
- lib/spec_led_ex/task_args.ex
- lib/spec_led_ex/** (ONE new module file for the shared validator, if you choose a new file over an existing home)
- test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs
- test/mix/tasks/spec_tasks_test.exs
- test/specled_ex/** (tests for the shared validator/task_args if placed there)
- .spec/specs/mix_tasks.spec.md
- .spec/realization_hashes.json

## Out of Scope (files)

- lib/spec_led_ex/next.ex, lib/spec_led_ex/prime.ex — the suggested_commands_with_protocol advisory is explicitly deferred
- docs/**, skills/**
- test/mix/tasks/spec_next_task_test.exs, test/mix/tasks/spec_prime_task_test.exs — specled_-0x4.1 owns them concurrently

## Out of Scope (intent)

- No behavior change to what constitutes a valid --base ref (C13 commit-only rule stays intact)
- No public API surface beyond the one shared validator (and the :ok | {:error, msg} TaskArgs shape if adopted)
- No new deps
- Verdict wording/grammar changes only if the spec.validate tier=usage alignment (scoped above) is taken; otherwise none

## Verification

- mix spec.check --no-run-commands passes on the stage branch
- One public validator: both Mix.Tasks.Spec.Check and BranchCheck call the SAME function for --base validation; the former private copies are gone (grep proves single definition)
- Existing pins green: test/mix/tasks/spec_check_test.exs and spec_tasks_test.exs (including the tier=usage pre-flight pins at :933/:954/:976 and the tier=validate pin at :607)
- CF6: print_verdict option access no longer order-sensitive (Keyword.get or equivalent); a test or the existing pins cover both orders OR the helper signatures are unified
- mix compile --warnings-as-errors; mix format --check-formatted

## Orchestrator note 2026-07-26
Corrected Allowed-touches glob typo test/spec_led_ex/** -> test/specled_ex/** (the repo's actual test dir); intent unchanged (tests for the shared validator/task_args).

Disposition confirmed: IMPLEMENT AS WRITTEN, do not close as moot (2026-07-25, post-review).

Context: a reviewer initially argued this ticket was moot because a single validation funnel in run/1 would delete validate_base!/2 outright. That argument depended on the verdict contract NOT being total — i.e. on some raise paths leaving `validate status=pass` as the last stdout line. That premise was DISPROVEN by execution (consolidated review Verification Log): record_evidence failure still prints the verdict (forced with chmod, exit 0), pre-report raises emit zero stdout, and the one window that could strand a misleading last line contains no reachable raise. The reviewer withdrew the moot recommendation on that basis.

With a total contract already in place, extracting one shared validator is the right resolution and this ticket stands as written.

Two adjacent duplication findings from the same review, same class, fold them in here:
- CF4: lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex:70-72 re-implements TaskArgs.validate!/3 own head match (`rest != [] or invalid != []`) purely to position the verdict print before the raise. They agree today (TaskArgs.validate!/3 has exactly one non-raising clause), but if the callee ever tolerates a leftover arg, spec.check would print result=fail, continue, and print result=pass — two verdict lines, violating the uniqueness clause. Note spec.validate solved the identical problem WITHOUT the duplicated predicate by printing inside the failure clause (spec.validate.ex:126-131); spec.check can simply match its sibling. Cleanest fix: convert TaskArgs.validate!/3 to :ok | {:error, message} so verdict and raise derive from one evaluation.
- CF6: print_verdict/2 in both task modules matches options positionally (`defp print_verdict("fail", tier: t, error_findings: n)`), so option ORDER is load-bearing and a missing key raises FunctionClauseError inside the one path whose purpose is to guarantee output. The two modules also define same-named/same-arity helpers with INCOMPATIBLE option lists (spec.check requires :tier, spec.validate rejects it), so copying a call site between the mirrored modules fails at runtime, not compile time. All six current call sites verified correct — latent only. Read options via Keyword.get/3.

Also related (separate finding, spec.validate.ex): sort_findings_for_display/1 re-types the exact four-element tuple of the pre-existing sort_key/1 about twenty lines above it. Compose rather than duplicate.

The ticket authorizes prose-only reconciliation edits to OTHER subject specs "ONLY when the spec gate demands them (branch_guard_missing_subject_update)". I refuted gate-demand for all four by execution. Per-file: `git checkout 2861c88 -- <file>` then `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --verbose`, for each of implementation_tier.spec.md, branch_guard.spec.md, status.spec.md, verification.spec.md. Then a combined run with ALL FOUR reverted. In every one of the five experiments the output was byte-identical to HEAD: `findings=3 (error=0 warning=0 info=3)`, the same three findings (branch_guard_missing_decision_update; branch_guard_missing_subject_update for lib/mix/tasks/spec.check.ex -> specled.api_boundary; branch_guard_missing_subject_update for lib/mix/tasks/spec.validate.ex -> specled.prose_guard), and `spec.check result=pass`. At no point did a branch_guard_missing_subject_update finding name specled.branch_guard, specled.status, specled.verification, or specled.implementation_tier. Sharpest case: implementation_tier.spec.md previously had NO reconciliation note at all (it is not in `git diff origin/main..2861c88 --name-only`); removing the newly added five-line note leaves the gate identically green, so that note is a pure unforced addition to a file the ticket does not allow touching. The three reworded notes are equally unforced — the pre-existing 0x4.2 prose kept the gate green on its own. All four edits are minimal and prose-only (no requirement or scenario bytes outside mix_tasks.spec.md), so the failure is authorization, not blast radius. Remedy: revert all four files to 2861c88 and re-run the gate; if the author wants the notes to reflect the added spec.validate pin, that is a request to widen this ticket's Allowed list, not something the gate demanded.
2. Reinforcing (same commit, same files): the three reworded notes now misdescribe the branch's dominant reason for touching spec_tasks_test.exs (see Reconciliation-note sweep). Even if the Allowed list were widened, the correct edit is to EXTEND the note to name both tokens, not to swap one true statement for a narrower one.

That is the same tier-dishonesty class 0x4.2 fixed for spec.check. The new scenario bullet is careful enough not to assert otherwise, and the scenario's `given` admits that path while the `then` stays silent about it, so this is not a contradiction — but it leaves the taxonomy lopsided. Worth a follow-up ticket. Relatedly, spec.validate.ex:125-132 still hand-rolls its own validate_args!/2 instead of using SpecLedEx.TaskArgs, which is the very duplication class this ticket attacks; CF4 named only spec.check, so it is out of scope here.
- The updated spec.validate min-strength pin at spec_tasks_test.exs:935-944 was NOT given `@tag spec: ["specled.tasks.verdict_line"]`, unlike the four spec.check pins the same commit tagged. Because build_command/2 resolves to whole files, the stub still executes it, so this is not a coverage hole — but per-test attribution (specled_-dn4) will not credit it to verdict_line even though it now pins a clause of that scenario.
- Defaulting choice in CF6: spec.check.ex:324 defaults `tier` to "usage" and spec.validate.ex:228 defaults it to "validate". A future call site that forgets :tier now silently mislabels the tier instead of crashing. Keyword.get/3 was the ticket's prescription, so this is compliant; consider Keyword.fetch! for :tier if silent mislabeling is worse than a crash on the guaranteed-output path.
- BranchCheck.run/3 error arm uses `Keyword.fetch!(opts, :base)` to rebuild the message tail. It is safe today (the error arm is only reachable when validate_base saw a non-nil, non-"HEAD" base, which implies the key is present), but it re-reads state the case already had; threading base through a local binding would remove the KeyError shape entirely.
- Minor behavior delta at the edges of the shared validator: the old private clauses guarded `when is_binary(base)` and would FunctionClauseError on a non-binary, non-nil base; the new `if base in [nil, "HEAD"]` interpolates whatever it gets. Unreachable from both current callers (OptionParser :string and the documented :base opt), so no C13 impact.
- Working tree left clean; all revert experiments fully reverted (`git status --short` empty). The pre-existing `stash@{0}` on a different branch was not created by this verification.

Reasoning: The verifier's five revert experiments were vacuous by construction and its sharpest case is inverted. SpecLedEx.ChangeAnalysis.changed_files/3 (lib/specled_ex/change_analysis.ex:83-95) unions scope_diff(base...HEAD) with working_tree_diff, staged_diff AND untracked_files, so `git checkout 2861c88 -- <file>` — which writes the reverted content to BOTH index and worktree — leaves the file in staged_diff and therefore still inside changed_files. Byte-identical output was guaranteed regardless of gate demand; this is the same working-tree-revert trap the verifier had already corrected once on specled_-0x4.1. I re-ran the experiment with COMMITTED reverts on a detached HEAD (the Spec-Drift trailer survives because Trailer.read/2 shells `git log base..HEAD --format=%B` over the whole range, per branch_check.ex:176) and the result splits the four files two ways: .spec/specs/implementation_tier.spec.md IS gate-demanded, and the other three are not.

Evidence (all `mix spec.check --no-run-commands --verbose`, base=origin/main):
- HEAD baseline: changed_files=15 findings=3 (error=0 info=3), spec.check result=pass. Reproduced exactly.
- Committed revert of ALL FOUR: changed_files=14 findings=4 (error=1 info=3), `spec.check result=fail tier=branch error_findings=1`, new finding `[ERROR] branch_guard_missing_subject_update lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex :: Changed file lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex impacts subject specs that were not updated: specled.implementation_tier`.
- Committed revert of the THREE reworded notes only (branch_guard, status, verification): findings=3 (error=0 info=3), result=pass — unchanged from baseline.

Root cause of the split, predictable without running anything: `git diff --name-only origin/main 2861c88` already contains branch_guard.spec.md, status.spec.md and verification.spec.md (0x4.2 edited all three), so reverting this commit's rewording leaves them modified vs origin/main and their subjects stay in changed_subject_ids. implementation_tier.spec.md is the ONE file of the four absent from that list — reverting it returns it to origin/main content, drops it out of changed_files entirely, and unmasks lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex -> specled.implementation_tier. The verifier identified that same asymmetry ("it is not in `git diff origin/main..2861c88 --name-only`") but drew the opposite conclusion from it, calling the note "a pure unforced addition"; in fact it is the only one of the four the gate compels.

Consequences for the verdict as written:
1. Gap 1 is wrong on implementation_tier.spec.md. That edit is fully authorized by the ticket's co-change clause: the gate demands it, the demanding finding code is exactly `branch_guard_missing_subject_update` as the clause names, the edit is five lines of prose in the Verification section with no requirement or scenario bytes, and it names lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex, which is genuinely in the diff and whose claim ("changes only its --base pre-flight validation seam; implementation-tier dispatch and hashing semantics remain unchanged") is true. Note that what silences the finding is the spec file being in changed_files at all, so a minimal prose note is precisely the "smallest edit that keeps the gate green".
2. The prescribed remedy is destructive. "Revert all four files to 2861c88 and re-run the gate" would convert a passing branch into `spec.check result=fail tier=branch error_findings=1`. Handing that to the implementer would have caused a second bounce.
3. Gap 1 stands, narrowed, on the other three files: branch_guard.spec.md, status.spec.md and verification.spec.md are outside Allowed touches and NOT gate-demanded (confirmed by committed revert), so their rewording is unauthorized.
4. Gap 2 is accurate and I sustain it. `git diff origin/main HEAD -- test/mix/tasks/spec_tasks_test.exs` is five hunks; `git diff --stat 2861c88 HEAD` shows this commit changed exactly ONE line of that file (the spec.validate min-strength pin at :943, tier=validate -> tier=usage). The other four hunks — the @tag additions at :587/:925/:945 and the spec.check tier=usage pins at :933/:954/:976 — pre-date this commit and came from 0x4.2. So the prior wording ("...the spec.check stdout verdict contract's usage-tier pre-flight rejection token") described the majority of the branch's reason for touching that file and was still true; swapping it for the spec.validate token alone is a net accuracy regression, exactly as the verifier characterized it. Since these three files should be reverted outright on authorization grounds, Gap 2 resolves as a side effect.

I did not re-audit the CODE deliverables; the verifier's findings there (one shared validator at branch_check.ex:646, C13 behavior-identical by execution, tier=usage alignment, CF4/CF6/sort_findings, 66 targeted tests green) are detailed, execution-backed, and I found nothing to contradict them.

Bounce reason: Re-issue the verification with the gate-demand analysis corrected. Specifically:
1. Retract the refutation for .spec/specs/implementation_tier.spec.md and record it as AUTHORIZED under the ticket's co-change clause, with the committed-revert evidence above (its removal yields error_findings=1 naming lib/specled_ex/branch_check.ex -> specled.implementation_tier and result=fail).
2. Retract the "revert all four files to 2861c88" remedy — it breaks the gate.
3. Restate Gap 1 as covering exactly three files: .spec/specs/branch_guard.spec.md, .spec/specs/status.spec.md, .spec/specs/verification.spec.md, each proven NOT gate-demanded by committed revert (result=pass, findings unchanged from baseline). Keep Gap 2 attached to those same three.
4.
